Geographic focus:
Europe (Eurozone / ECB), with secondary reference to US (Federal Reserve) and Japan (Bank of Japan)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references past ECB rate hikes and ongoing Middle East conflict backdrop
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — December ECB hike, October 29 ECB meeting, upcoming Fed and BoJ meetings
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Citi's March 2027 hike call, inflation not returning to target until late 2027

Synopsis:
Goldman Sachs, Citi, and Barclays all expect the ECB to hike rates again in December, driven by persistent inflation above the 2% target and renewed energy price pressures stemming from Middle East conflict and US-Iran tensions pushing crude above $100/bbl. Citi goes further, penciling in an additional hike in March 2027. Markets are pricing a ~94% probability of a December ECB move. Secondary focus is on the upcoming Fed and BoJ meetings, which could reinforce a global monetary tightening backdrop.
